best_for: Students interested in electronics and engineering
Makers who want to build physical projects
not_for: Students who prefer only software/screen-based coding
target_audience.who_should_take_foundation_first: No prior electronics experience needed, but basic block coding experience helps.

system_requirements.hardware: A computer for coding and simulations. (Optional: Physical Arduino kit).

overview.positioning: An exciting introduction to hardware, circuits, and programming the physical world.
overview.short_description: Bring your code to life! Learn how to build basic circuits, wire up LEDs and sensors, and program virtual (or physical) robots using Arduino and Tinkercad.

key_facts.capstone: Design a Virtual Smart Home System or Robot Controller

what_you_will_be_able_to_do: Understand basic electronic circuits (power, ground, components)
Use Tinkercad Circuits to simulate wiring safely
Write code to control LEDs and motors

why_now.industry_shift: The Internet of Things (IoT) means hardware and software are merging.
why_now.ai_impact: Robots are the physical bodies for AI brains.
why_now.business_demand: Hardware engineering remains a critical, high-demand field.
why_now.career_opportunity: Excellent hands-on introduction to mechanical and electrical engineering.

learning_outcomes: WIRE: Build safe, functional circuits using breadboards.
SIMULATE: Use digital tools to test circuits before building.
CODE: Program microcontrollers to interact with hardware.
SENSE: Use environmental sensors to trigger actions.

core_tools.what_student_learns: Wiring without risk of short circuits

stages.name: Code
stages.desc: Writing the logic for the microcontroller.

best_practices: Red wire is for Power (5V), Black wire is for Ground (GND).
Always use a resistor with an LED so it doesn't burn out.
Simulate your circuit first before building it in real life.

common_mistakes.professional_approach: Always trace the path of electricity carefully before pressing 'Start Simulation'.

common_mistakes.why_it_happens: LEDs have polarity (positive and negative sides).
common_mistakes.professional_approach: Ensure the longer leg (anode) goes to power and the shorter (cathode) to ground.

career_paths.employer_expectations: Basic understanding of electronics and microcontrollers.

final_deliverables: A fully programmed virtual hardware project.

assessment.criteria: Circuit runs without simulated damage, code executes intended logic.

certification.title: Junior Robotics Basics Certificate
certification.criteria: Complete the final Tinkercad circuit project.

not_covered: Soldering, advanced robotics math, physical construction (course is simulation focused).

faq.question: Do I need to buy a robotics kit?
faq.answer: No! We use Tinkercad Circuits to simulate everything online for free. You can buy a physical Arduino kit later if you wish.

faq.question: Is this safe?
faq.answer: 100% safe. Because we do it virtually first, there is no risk of shocks or broken parts.

modules.module_purpose: Understand how electricity flows and how to build simple circuits.

lessons.what_is_taught: Batteries, LEDs, and basic electrical flow.
lessons.why_it_matters: Fundamental rule: electricity needs a complete circle to flow.
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a simple coin-cell battery and LED circuit in Tinkercad.

lessons.what_is_taught: How breadboards connect components without soldering.
lessons.why_it_matters: The standard tool for all prototyping.
lessons.what_learner_does: Wires multiple LEDs cleanly on a breadboard.
Adds switches and resistors to their LED circuit.

modules.hands_on_practice: Build a circuit with a switch that controls 3 LEDs at once.

modules.module_purpose: Introduce microcontrollers to add logic and programming to circuits.

lessons.what_is_taught: The parts of an Arduino board (Pins, USB, Power).
lessons.why_it_matters: This is the computer that will control the hardware.
lessons.what_learner_does: Connects an Arduino to a breadboard in Tinkercad.
Writes a program to make an LED blink on and off.
lessons.expected_outcome: A flashing LED controlled by code.

lessons.what_learner_does: Programs Red, Yellow, and Green LEDs to act like a real traffic light.

modules.hands_on_practice: Program a customized police-light flashing sequence.
modules.assignment: Submit the Traffic Light project link.
modules.expected_outcome: Ability to control hardware outputs with code.

modules.module_purpose: Make the Arduino react to the environment and create physical movement.

lessons.why_it_matters: Allows robots to understand their environment.
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a smart nightlight that turns on when the room gets dark.

lessons.what_is_taught: Including the Servo library and controlling angles.
lessons.why_it_matters: The basics of robotic arms and steering.
lessons.what_learner_does: Programs a servo motor to sweep back and forth like a windshield wiper.

lessons.why_it_matters: Synthesizes all learning into a full robotic system.
lessons.what_learner_does: Designs a system where a motor moves based on sensor input (e.g., a waving robot when someone gets close).

modules.hands_on_practice: Build the Smart Robot capstone project.
modules.assignment: Submit the final Tinkercad simulation link.
modules.expected_outcome: Ability to integrate sensors and motors into a programmed system.
